A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dual-attention MILP backbone. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction, solver-performance, branching, MIPLIB generalization, and architectural-analysis results in Sections 4.1–4.5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds advanced-backbone comparisons, inference-time measurements, and parameter-sensitivity studies in Section 4.5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed backbone retains parallel linearized self-attention, coefficient-aware sparse cross-attention, residual normalization, feature fusion, and the same downstream prediction heads. The revised sparse-attention definition corrects its mathematical specification without establishing a change to the intended procedure. Newly introduced architectures are comparators.

E1.justification: Both versions cover foldable/unfoldable instance prediction; IP, WA, MIS, and CA element prediction; SC, CA, CFL, and MIS branching with larger transfer instances; and the same 215 MIPLIB instances. The added comparisons and parameter studies use retained datasets and tasks. MIPLIB moves to Appendix A.3.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 adds evaluated OPTFM, MAGCN, GCON, and GNN-SSM comparators across binary prediction and downstream predict-and-search experiments. Polynormer corresponds to v1's bipartite BGT comparison on WA, whose scores are retained, and gains comparisons in other retained experiments. BGNN, BGAT, BGNN+self, Gurobi, and the PaS/Apollo comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce WA-based backbone-depth selection and method-specific PaS settings, alongside new depth/width sweeps and per-instance inference timing. The reported classification metric set also contracts from six metrics to four, omitting balanced accuracy and error counts. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original backbone configurations and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds joint depth/width sensitivity on WA (Table 18), depth-selection analyses for advanced backbones (Tables 21–22), and inference-overhead analysis (Appendix A.4). These examine capacity sensitivity, comparator configuration, and computational cost. Existing embedding, gradient, probability-distribution, component-ablation, and MIPLIB analyses remain, partly relocated to Appendix A.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly states that each branching policy is evaluated under five random seeds per instance. The corresponding tree-size values and uncertainty entries are unchanged, so this establishes additional disclosure, not an increase in runs. Both versions already report five training repetitions and standard deviations for the depth experiment.

E6.justification: New Tables 6–8 add extensive comparator results: WA MCC is 0.8411 for the proposed model versus 0.8022 for GNN-SSM, while IP MCC favors GNN-SSM, 0.0186 versus 0.0178. Timing and parameter-grid results are also added. Matched original results largely retain their values, while balanced-accuracy and error-count entries disappear. The additional PG/PI tables are not reconciled with retained Table 3 and do not establish performance changes over v1.

T1.justification: v1 defines attention scores as exp(pij) while asserting they vanish for zero coefficients; v2 explicitly assigns zero to non-edges, correcting that mathematical inconsistency. Section 2 also corrects the variable/constraint embedding initialization maps. No new theorem, proof, or substantial theoretical development is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an element-centric dual-attention backbone that overcomes local GNN representation limitations across instance-, element-, and solving-state-level tasks. The introduction and conclusion retain the claims of improved prediction and generalization. Rewritten abstract wording and additional comparisons principally change presentation and supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explicit discussion of unresolved behavior on extremely large, label-imbalanced industrial problems and much of v1's future-work discussion. It newly characterizes measured inference overhead as modest and qualifies performance on IP against advanced comparators. The principal explanations concerning global interactions, deeper representations, and MIPLIB generalization remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3.4 newly specifies MIS branching sizes and edge probability; C.2 specifies IP/WA test indices 9900–9999 where v1 named a validation folder, without establishing whether the actual split changed. New comparator depths and PaS parameters are documented. Existing hardware, training settings, and code URL remain, but the explicit Gurobi v12.0.1 disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: v2 discusses OPTFM and MAGCN as concurrent MILP architectures and GCON/GNN-SSM as advanced graph comparators. It adds their citations and Geng et al. (2025), while removing v1's application-example references 8–13. Polynormer was already cited and evaluated. These extend the existing research positioning without redefining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively condensed or rewritten. Probability analysis, ablations, and MIPLIB evaluation move into a new additional-results appendix; advanced-architecture comparisons become a main section. References move before the appendices, and front matter and section organization are revised.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column journal layout to a two-column conference layout. v1's detailed architecture/application Figure 2 is removed, while other figures are resized or relocated. Classification tables lose two columns, v1 Table 4's averages enter v2 Table 3, and new comparison, timing, sensitivity, and configuration tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly BGNN-based evaluation, v2 provides broader architectural comparisons, capacity checks, measured inference costs, and useful reproducibility details. These strengthen support for the existing contribution. The gains are tempered by the removed limitations discussion and reporting inconsistencies: Table 22 selects Polynormer with MCC 0.7498, but Table 6 reports 0.7408, and the additional PG/PI results are not reconciled with retained Table 3. The net improvement is therefore limited.
